summary: Igor I Sikorsky Memorial Airport (BDR) is a medium-sized public airport located in Stratford, Connecticut, serving the greater Bridgeport metropolitan area. It is named after the legendary aviation pioneer Igor Sikorsky, who conducted his first successful helicopter flight from this very airfield in 1939. The airport remains a notable site in aviation history and serves as a convenient gateway for travelers in southwestern Connecticut.
faqs:
Q: Who was Igor Sikorsky, and why is the airport named after him?
A: Igor Sikorsky was a pioneering aviation engineer known for designing some of the earliest successful helicopters and large fixed-wing aircraft. The airport honors him because he conducted his first successful helicopter flight from this location in 1939.

Q: What is the airport primarily used for today?
A: BDR serves as a general aviation and corporate airport, accommodating private aircraft, charter flights, flight training, and some limited commercial operations for the Bridgeport-Stamford region.

Q: Are there commercial passenger flights from BDR?
A: Scheduled commercial passenger service is very limited. Most travelers use the airport for private, corporate, or charter aviation rather than major airline routes.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: The airport features fixed-base operators (FBOs), fuel services, aircraft maintenance, hangar rentals, and a control tower operated during active hours.
transport_tips: The airport is located just off Interstate 95, making it easily accessible by car from Bridgeport, New Haven, and surrounding Fairfield County towns. On-site parking is available near the terminal and FBOs, and rideshare services such as Uber and Lyft operate in the area. Public transportation options are limited, so arranging a private vehicle or taxi in advance is recommended for most visitors.
local_tip: If you have time before a flight, visit the nearby Sikorsky Memorial Bridge or check out the Igor Sikorsky exhibit at the airport to appreciate the historic significance of the site where helicopter aviation took its first practical flight.
